briefdescription.para: Nonlocal viscosities $ \eta_K $ of the nonlocal balances.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the state variable array.

simplesect.para: Nonlocal viscosity of each nonlocal variable, the damping coefficient of the damped hyperbolic (or, with zero micro-inertia, parabolic) balance \[ m_K\,\ddot{\bar{N}}_K + \eta_K\,\dot{\bar{N}}_K + \bar{N}_K - c_K\,\nabla^2\bar{N}_K = L_K . \]

Zero by default, which is the quasi-static model. Unlike the small-strain Marmot::Materials::MaterialGradientEnhancedHypoElastic::getNonlocalViscosity, which is pure virtual, this default lets a material that is only ever used implicitly leave it alone.

briefdescription.para: Nonlocal micro-inertias $ m_K $ of the nonlocal balances.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the state variable array.

simplesect.para: Nonlocal micro-inertia of each nonlocal variable, in units of [time]^2.

The default is zero, the quasi-static model in which a nonlocal field is first order in time and integrated by its viscosity alone. A derived class opts in to the damped hyperbolic balance by overriding this, mirroring Marmot::Materials::MaterialGradientEnhancedHypoElastic::getNonlocalMicroInertia.

briefdescription.para: Abstract base class for gradient-enhanced (implicit-gradient) materials in the finite strain regime.

detaileddescription.para:
nNonlocal
Number of nonlocal variables $ \bar{N}_K $, $ K = 1 \dots n_\mathrm{nonlocal} $: one for a scalar nonlocal damage driver, six for a nonlocal strain tensor (GM7).
The finite-strain counterpart of Marmot::Materials::MaterialGradientEnhancedHypoElastic: the displacement field is coupled to nNonlocal nonlocal fields $ \bar{N}_K $, each governed by the additional balance equation \[ \bar{N}_K - c_K\,\nabla^2\bar{N}_K = L_K(\boldsymbol{F},\,\bar{\boldsymbol{N}}), \qquad c_K = R_K^2, \] where $ L_K $ is the local driving force reported in ConstitutiveResponse::L and $ R_K $ the nonlocal radius reported in ConstitutiveResponse::nonLocalRadius.

Quantities of the nonlocal space are Eigen vectors of size nNonlocal, as in the small-strain interface; a tangent mixing a spatial tensor with a nonlocal variable is one Fastor tensor per nonlocal variable, so that a consumer evaluates for each nonlocal variable exactly the expression it would evaluate for a single one.

simplesect.para: The nonlocal balance is formulated in the material (reference) configuration. Consumers take the gradients with respect to $ \boldsymbol{X} $ and integrate over the reference volume, so $ c_K $ is a material constant and is neither pushed forward nor weighted by $ J $. The stress, in contrast, is the Kirchhoff stress $ \boldsymbol{\tau} = J\,\boldsymbol{\sigma} $, which is what integrating against the reference volume requires. A nonlocal variable that stands for a tensor (the six components of a nonlocal strain) must therefore be referred to a frame that a superposed rigid rotation does not change, e.g. the frame of the polar rotation (see GradientEnhancedCorotationalWrapper).

There is **no slot for $ \partial c_K/\partial\bar{N} $**: a material with damage-dependent interactions (see MarmotDecreasingInteractions) can report the current $ c_K $, but not its derivative, so its consistent tangent would be incomplete.
